summary: Unexpected burst-credit depletion during parallel model warmups causing throttled requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in throttled requests after they initiated parallel model warmups across multiple routes in their dedicated pool. The customer expects warmup traffic to be treated as low-priority and not to exhaust burst credits used by latency-sensitive routes.

Impact:
- ~15% of production inference calls returned 429-like throttle responses within a 10-minute window during warmups.
- Customer observed elevated tail latency and queued requests on priority routes while warmup traffic was running.
- Affects core user flows in Nimbus AI (real-time ranking and chat).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1
- Prod traffic: steady baseline ~250 req/s, warmups launched ~120 parallel workers across 6 routes
- Models warmed: redwood/gpt-compat-3.8 (long-context), open/reward-7B (shorter-context)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Schedule parallel warmup script across 6 routes using short-lived API keys.
2) Each worker submits 30 simultaneous short sequence generation requests to prefill KV cache.
3) Observe increased 429s and throttle headers appearing on unrelated low-latency routes.

Observed headers and logs excerpt:
- x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- x-rate-limit-reset: 15
- x-throttle-reason: burst_credit_exhausted
- Gateway logs: repeated 429s from multiple route shards correlated with warmup start time: 2026-03-10T15:05:12Z

Customer expectation:
Warmup activity should either be accounted in a separate burst window or be deprioritized so it cannot deplete production burst credits for customer routes.

Requested outcome:
- Clarify how dedicated-pool burst credits are consumed during concurrent warmups.
- Recommended config or best-practice to avoid production route throttling during warmups (config samples, backoff patterns, or dedicated warmup weight).
comments: 2026-03-10 15:20 - Ava Moreno (customer): We kicked off the warmup at 15:05 UTC and started seeing 429s on our chat route ~30s after. We have screenshots of the throttle headers and can share request traces.

2026-03-10 15:45 - Liam Chen (support): Thanks Ava — opening an investigation with SRE and rate-limiter team. Can you confirm whether warmup traffic used the same API keys / subaccount as production? Also any differences in connection reuse (http2) vs fresh connections?

2026-03-10 16:10 - Ava Moreno (customer): Warmup used short-lived keys generated from the same tenant and subaccount. We did use separate worker hosts, each maintaining persistent HTTP/2 connections to the edge.

2026-03-10 18:02 - SRE (investigation): Initial hypothesis: burst-token accounting currently aggregates at tenant level for dedicated pools; parallel warmups using many short-lived keys consumed tenant burst credit quickly. Investigating whether health checks or preflight requests also increment counters.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Liam Chen (support): Suggested temporary mitigation: stagger warmup workers and reduce parallelism to keep concurrent inflight requests < 20 per route; consider using a flagged warmup key if available. Customer to test and report back.

2026-03-11 11:15 - Ava Moreno (customer): Tried reducing parallelism to 8 workers and warmup duration spread across 10 minutes — throttles dropped to normal levels. Will wait for engineering analysis for permanent fix.

2026-03-12 10:00 - SRE: Found that health-check probes from autoscaler also execute short model queries that consume burst capacity when model instances spin up; autoscaler probes run concurrently with warmup leading to double accounting. Opening infra PR to separate probe traffic accounting.
investigation_notes:
Findings so far:
- Token-bucket accounting is applied at tenant scope by default for dedicated pools; route-level isolation is enabled only when explicit per-route quota separation is configured.
- Short-lived API keys that reuse the same tenant/subaccount share the same refill window and burst credit. Rapid fan-out of keys makes refill appear instantaneous but depletes the tenant token bucket.
- Autoscaler/health-check probes execute lightweight model calls from control plane hosts; these calls are currently counted against the same quota and are concurrent with customer warmups.
- Connection multiplexing (HTTP/2) reduced per-connection windowing but did not prevent aggregate burst depletion.

Hypotheses:
1) Combined effect of parallel warmup workers + autoscaler probes caused temporary tenant-level burst exhaustion, manifesting as throttles for other routes.
2) Short-lived keys triggered per-key refill smoothing that did not distribute burst capacity as expected across windows.

Next steps:
- Confirm quota accounting logs and request traces for the exact token debit timestamps (SRE to query rate-limiter ledger).
- Reproduce in staging with dedicated pool replica using same warmup pattern and autoscaler enabled.
- Evaluate and implement two immediate mitigations: 1) document and recommend staggered warmups in Best Practices; 2) add optional warmup flag or separate warmup quota scope for dedicated pools.
- Infra PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123) to avoid counting autoscaler probe traffic against tenant burst credits; target rollout to canary on 2026-03-18.
resolution: Workaround delivered: customer staggered warmup workers and limited parallel inflight requests which eliminated immediate throttles. SRE confirmed autoscaler probe accounting fix in PR #4123; will roll out canary next week. Follow-up items: create dedicated warmup quota guidance in Console docs, add an opt-in warmup flag for dedicated pools, and document per-route isolation config. Ticket will remain open pending PR canary and documentation updates.
